meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you two chatting here?

examples.text: А я вот себе туфли новые купил.
examples.trans: And I just bought myself new shoes.

examples.text: Вы с Викой расстались, и она сразу кого-то нашла?
examples.trans: You and Vika broke up, and she immediately found someone?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'called', paired with 'позвать'.

examples.trans: Did you call for me?
What's your name?
My name is Lyosha.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!
The rookie has returned!
Vika, wait!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

examples.text: Тем более, что ты уже начал.
examples.trans: Especially since you have already started.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'spoke, said', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: We need to talk!
Go to our place, we will talk tonight.

examples.text: Моя бывшая беременна, говорит, что не от меня.
examples.trans: My ex is pregnant and says it is not mine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
Who told you?

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: She is a good one you have.
Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.
Maybe she was joking?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.

examples.text: Кате всё равно правду не расскажешь.
examples.trans: You cannot tell Katya the truth anyway.
Alright, it is settled, we are going.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'knows'.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!

examples.text: Я узнала о тебе много нового.
examples.trans: I learned a lot of new things about you.

examples.text: Даже не знаешь человека и защищаешь его.
examples.trans: You do not even know the man and you defend him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It turns out we are friends in misfortune.
Katya and I broke up.
We are exchanging curious facts, after all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'why', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Why did you tell her everything?
What have you come for?
What's that for?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?
In a divorce, two people are always at fault.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to tell (a story, news)', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Обо мне ведь ничего не рассказал.
examples.trans: After all, you told her nothing about me.

examples.text: Настя, ну я не могу тебе рассказать.
examples.trans: Nastya, well I cannot tell you.
Kostik told me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
Vika, wait!
We need to talk!

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Витя, в ресторане всё в порядке?
examples.trans: Vitya, is everything alright in the restaurant?
I am the head chef of this restaurant.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'рядок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Витя, в ресторане всё в порядке?
examples.trans: Vitya, is everything alright in the restaurant?
Now let's go through everything in order.
Everything is in complete order.

meanings.en: after all, still, all the same
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'ё-таки').

examples.text: Я всё-таки решила с тобой поговорить.
examples.trans: I decided to talk with you after all.
He came after all.
Maybe we'll go after all?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'decided', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Вот поэтому он решил с тобой расстаться.
examples.trans: That is why he decided to break up with you.

examples.text: Я всё-таки решила с тобой поговорить.
examples.trans: I decided to talk with you after all.
The court has decided.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: We need to talk!
Go to our place, we will talk tonight.
I need to talk with the doctor.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This is not your child.

examples.text: Ну чей это ребёнок, если не твой?
examples.trans: Well whose child is it, if not yours?

examples.text: Убедиться в том, что ребёнок твой, очень просто.
examples.trans: Making sure that the child is yours is very simple.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('second (afternoon)').

examples.text: Лена, а кто автор всех этих шедевров?
examples.trans: Lena, and who is the author of all these masterpieces?
Your second wife is in the dining room.
This is my second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Is Den married?
His wife left him.
My wife is being monitored by you.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hall' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Who told you?

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Обо мне ведь ничего не рассказал.
examples.trans: After all, you told her nothing about me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'знакомить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will introduce', paired with 'знакомить'.

examples.trans: I'll introduce you.
Introduce me to him.

examples.text: О, а вот и мой заместитель! Пойдёмте, я вас познакомлю.
examples.trans: Oh, and here's my deputy! Come on, I'll introduce you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is standing', paired with 'постоять'.

examples.trans: Congratulations, daddy, a real bouncing boy.
I'm standing here.

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That simply cannot be!
Maybe she was joking?

examples.text: А может, это ребёнок не от меня, правда?
examples.trans: Maybe this child really is not mine?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'спринять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take / perceive'.

examples.text: Она может воспринять это как оскорбление.
examples.trans: She might take this as an insult.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и воспринять вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to take on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How noble.
As a subordinate.

examples.text: Это какую правду Кате не расскажешь?
examples.trans: What truth can you not tell Katya?

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'insult' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Она может воспринять это как оскорбление.
examples.trans: She might take this as an insult.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть оскорбление.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always insult.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vika, wait!
We need to talk!
I know that you are pregnant!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!
Who told you?

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

meanings.en: to have to, to be forced to
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'йтись'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'it will be necessary', paired with 'приходиться'.

examples.trans: I'm going to have to torture you.
We had to wait a long time.

examples.text: Ты что, очкарик, не понимаешь? Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask, to beg', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Она просила меня забрать её анализы.
examples.trans: She asked me to pick up her test results.

examples.text: А меня Виктория просила ничего не говорить.
examples.trans: And Victoria asked me not to say anything.

examples.text: Познакомь, а то мне придётся Катю просить.
examples.trans: Introduce us, or else I will have to ask Katya.

meanings.en: to be, to spend a little time
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'stay', paired with 'быть'.

examples.trans: I want to be alone.
Let's stay here a little longer.

examples.text: Забирайте и уходите. Я хочу побыть одна.
examples.trans: Take it and go. I want to be alone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is that I am here.
What does that have to do with this?
Lena, what are we doing here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: And where is the daughter right now?
I will do everything right now, Chef.

examples.text: Ты побудь здесь, я сейчас с ней поговорю.
examples.trans: You stay here, I will go talk to her right now.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: She is a good one you have.

examples.text: Как у тебя дела, всё хорошо?
examples.trans: How are you doing, is everything fine?
Alright, I will wait here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
